description: Enlarge an EXISTING clip (Topaz, passed through fal): same shot, same length, same sound — more pixels. There is no prompt here; nothing is re-imagined, the frames are scaled. The source is the clip of a generated-video row. Both the length and the source height are measured server-side before anything is charged, and a source too tall for the larger factor is refused rather than run. ASYNCHRONOUS: a new video row comes back as pending; poll it with lab_job_status. Costs credits when called without get_cost.

faktor.description: How many times larger, per side. Omit for the smaller one. Whichever you pick, the RESULT has to stay inside the published rate tiers — a source too tall for the factor you asked for is refused by name, with the ceiling in the message, instead of billing a run nobody can price. What the tier costs is in lab_list_models and in the preflight, not here.

get_cost.description: `true` returns the published rate per output second per tier and your balance WITHOUT scaling and without spending anything — NOT a total. Two things decide the amount and both are measured server-side: the length of the source, and the height of the RESULT (source height times factor) which picks the tier. The answer also says which tiers are measured and which are catalog values — the same distinction lab_list_models makes. The real amount comes back with the actual call.

video_id.description: Generated-video id (from lab_animate/lab_job_status/lab_review_queue) — positive integer as string. The row must already have its clip; a run still pending is refused, and nothing is charged for asking.

name: lab_upscale
title: Upscale Clip
